functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Thin, deep muscle beneath the rhomboids; despite lying in the back, its rib-elevating action makes it functionally a respiratory accessory muscle rather than a shoulder-girdle muscle.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe in the sagittal plane, just medial to the medial border of the scapula, over the upper posterior thoracic wall (around the 2nd rib); needle advanced in-plane in a caudocranial direction.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Local anesthetic is deposited between this muscle and the rib/external intercostal muscle beneath it -- i.e. directly deep to this muscle's own belly, distinguishing it from most other fascial-plane blocks in the region, which target planes between other muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: This thin muscle is seen deep to the rhomboid major and trapezius, medial to the scapula, running obliquely down onto the upper ribs; a cadaveric dye study confirmed spread reaching the rhomboid major, erector spinae, and the deep fascia of subscapularis/serratus anterior as well as the intercostal nerves.
structures_at_risk: pleura and underlying lung (pneumothorax), deep to the rib this muscle inserts on
dorsal scapular vessels and nerve, which run in the region between the rhomboids and the muscle
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Genuine, muscle-specific finding: the serratus posterior superior intercostal plane (SPSIP) block is a real, named ultrasound-guided technique that injects directly around this muscle's own belly (between it and the underlying rib), described first in a cadaveric dye-spread study and case series and since reported for rib-fracture and thoracic-surgery analgesia. This is a genuine nerve-block target rather than a BoNT motor point -- no motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for BoNT injection into this muscle was found.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Tulgar S et al (2023) 'Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block: A Technical Report on the Description of a Novel Periparavertebral Block for Thoracic Pain', Cureus 15(2):e34582, doi:10.7759/cureus.34582 -- original cadaveric dye-spread study and case series describing the block; Gundogdu O et al (2026) J Cardiothorac Vasc Anesth, doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.06.043 -- case series applying the block for isolated rib fractures (transducer/needle-path detail used here); Alver S et al (2024) A A Pract 18(4):e01773, doi:10.1213/XAA.0000000000001773 -- case report of the block for pectus excavatum repair
